title: Online LLM Personalization from Pairwise Preferences Across Users
abstract: arXiv:2610.17203v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Large language models can answer the same question in different styles, but users' preferred styles are hidden and vary across users and questions. We study inference-time personalization through online selection from a fixed set of prompts, each representing a persona. Users arrive sequentially, each asks a short sequence of questions, and the system displays two responses per question and observes one pairwise choice. We formulate this interaction as a variant of the contextual dueling bandit problem in which the learner starts without preference data, adapts within each session, and exploits information shared across users. The objective is to minimize cumulative strong regret, summing the utility gaps of both displayed responses relative to the user's best response among the available options. translated_title: 基于跨用户成对偏好的在线大语言模型个性化
translated_abstract: 大语言模型可以用不同的风格回答同一个问题，但用户偏好的风格是隐藏的，且因用户和问题而各不相同。我们研究推理时的个性化问题，即从一个固定的提示词集合（每个提示词代表一种人格角色）中进行在线选择。用户依次到来，每位用户提出一小段序列的问题，系统对每个问题展示两个回答，并观察一次成对选择。我们将这种交互形式化为上下文决斗老虎机问题的一个变体：学习者起初没有任何偏好数据，能在每个会话内进行自适应，并利用跨用户共享的信息。目标是最小化累积强遗憾（strong regret），即所展示的两个回答相对于用户在可用选项中最佳回答的效用差距之和。我们做出了两项贡献：第一，我们提出了该问题，并发布了一个可复现的偏好基准和数据集，该基准围绕教学辅导场景构建……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文将基于成对偏好反馈的大语言模型推理时个性化形式化为上下文决斗老虎机问题的变体，提出一种无需初始偏好数据、可在会话内自适应并利用跨用户共享信息的在线选择方法，以最小化累积强遗憾。
en_tdlr: This paper formulates inference-time LLM personalization from pairwise preference feedback as a variant of the contextual dueling bandit problem, enabling online prompt selection without initial preference data, within-session adaptation, and cross-user information sharing to minimize cumulative strong regret.
